intended_object: The position (arity) family B : A → Type of the polynomial functor (container) whose final coalgebra is the type of interaction trees. A `ret` node has no children, a `tau` node has one, and a `vis α e` node has one child for each element of the response type α. This comes from the docstring and from its use in `ITree.P := ⟨ITree.shape ε ρ, ITree.children⟩`.
explanation:
The definition gives the standard container presentation of interaction trees (Xia et al.), which has three node shapes:
- `ret v` has an empty set of positions: `ULift (Fin2 0)` is empty.
- `tau` has exactly one position: `ULift (Fin2 1)` has exactly one element.
- `vis α e` has one position per element of α.

This matches the intended coinductive type `ret v | tau t | vis e (k : α → ITree)`. The `ULift` wrapping is only needed to land in `Type u1`, so universe handling has no mathematical effect.

The definition is specific to the interaction-tree functor, so it cannot be too narrow. Mathlib supplies the general machinery (`PFunctor`, `PFunctor.M`) but has no interaction-tree functor of its own, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.

One could also argue it is just a component of the bundled `PFunctor`. Even so, it is the arity part of a genuine mathematical object (a container), and it is correct.
